steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Beat peanut butter, butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until well blended. Beat in egg until well combined. Mix in milk and vanilla. Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl; stir into peanut butter mixture until incorporated.
Roll tablespoonfuls of dough into balls. Place cookies 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Press each ball once with fork tines.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Joey’s Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: The best peanut butter cookies are made with this easy recipe that uses a double dose of peanut butter for fluffy cookies that melt in your mouth.

review.reviewBody: A lot of people love this recipe. Some do not. I think it is really good. You don't need to add any extra flour to the recipe. I will admit the batter is a bit more slack than a lot of people are used to. Use a 1-ounce metal cookie scooper and you will have no problem with the dough. Use a fork dipped in water to make the criss-cross design. I did refrigerate some of the dough after scooping it and I found that it is actually easier to get a more uniform, pretty criss-cross design if you do it straight from the bowl without chilling. The chilled dough did work okay, but it did crack on the sides and I had to push the sides together to make a uniform circle. Also, check you oven temperature. You cannot go by the time given. Everyone's oven is different. I baked mine at 350 degrees for 11 minutes and they were underdone and delicate/broke apart. But, I baked a second batch for 16 minutes and they are perfect. They don't fall apart and are still soft in the center and crisp on the edges with nice color. I bake professionally for an upscale private club and none of our recipes have time listed. You have to be able to tell when it's done by how it looks and feels. Baking can be tempermental. Mixing methods, ingredients, environment, humidity, and a whole host of other things affect your recipe. The same recipe can come out differently every time if you don't pay attention to things like the weather, brands, heavy footfalls, etc.

Just made these and they are DELISH! Easy to make and come out beautiful IF you follow directions.I use Jif peanut butter, butter and milk.Blend well in Kitchen Aid ( or other mixer)…Add the sugars (mix well) then add egg and vanilla.I mixed up the flour, powder and salt and added to peanut butter mixture. Just until combined.The dough will be sticky, but not impossible to roll. I do put onto parchment paper, cross cross fork design. Then I added A mixture of salt and sugar and sprinkled over the cookie!Please don’t allow those that add a bad review on here keep you from trying these. THE BEST PEANUT BUTTER FLAVOR that MELTS in your MOUTH!

This is a wonderful recipe, thank you!

Not sure why people rated one star.

I mixed according to ingredients and encountered the same issue with dough being too soft. To avoid soft dough refrigerate for about 20 -30 min to firm up to imprint with fork for cute design.
I added an additional 1/2 C flour after all was mixed which worked well for me (I am not high altitude). I did not keep track of baking time, just waited for edges to brown, they were perfect.
I made a couple batches, left them in oven to crisp up (these were our favorite)

I'm so happy to see a peanut butter cookie that does not call for shortening. This is definitely a keeper.
Thanks again!

I used crunchy peanut butter. I also only had half n half, so I used 1.5 Tbs H&H mixed with 1.5Tbs water. I also added 3/4 C chocolate chips, without changing the recipe. I would add 1 tsp of salt -- just shy salt, and peanut butter cookies need a kick of salty with the sweet. Texture light and fluffy. TIP: Do not over cream or over stir. Cookies will be flat and runny.

Just took a batch out of the oven, they came out great!! The only thing I changed was using chunky peanut butter and I put the dough in fridge for 10 minutes. Used a small cookie scoup and got 48 cookies...
This recipe is the bomb.I made them with Gluten free flour and they were soft and delicious. I also chilled the batter before baking , definitely a keeper !

These are perfect...we made sone exactly like the recipe called for and some with different chips in them...peanut butter chips and milk chocolate chips...all were amazing and soft. The milk chocolate chips were the best because the chocolate cut down of the peanut butter a bit. Additionally, we took about 2 cups worth and ground them in the processor with about 4 oz of cream cheese, rolled them into balls, and dipped them into chocolaelte for little truffles...best we have ever had...beats making reese's peanut butter centers. Best of luck!

My whole family loved these. I scooped the dough with a cookie scoop and flattened slightly with a floured fork and topped with a hershey's kiss. awesome. they stayed soft, and froze really well. thank you!

I loved this recipe! The only things I did different:
1. Set my oven to 350 and figured out 7 mins was best for my oven after burning the bottoms of the first batch. If I had set it to 375 they would have all been scorched black hockey pucks. Recipe times are always just a suggestion since so many factors affect the outcome.
2. Dipped my fork in sugar before making the criss cross pattern on top. It helped the dough to not stick to the fork since the dough is a little wetter than most cookie recipes.
3. Added a bag of Heath chocolate and toffee baking bits. This recipe would be just as delicious without them, but the addition of toffee and chocolate was awesome.

These cookies are absolutely DELICIOUS and not dry! I baked mine @350 for 12 minutes.

The dough is a little loose. I only ever bake one tray of cookies at a time, and refrigerated the remainder. The next day, the consistency was perfect and could easily be rolled into balls (also then rolled in sugar).

I'd recommend refrigerating the dough for at least a few hours PRIOR to baking.

This is my 3rd time making these, I love the recipe. I add 6oz of mini chocolate chips to them and cook them a few minutes longer to get the edges a little crispy. They never seemed done at 10 mins, could be my oven
Great cookie recipe.
I loved this recipe it was easy to follow did not make a lot of dishes .we accidentally put the dry ingredients in the wet ingredients bowl but it still worked I will continue making this recipe
Was looking for that crisp edge with chewy center... this is not it! Not bad, just not great.
Good but thick and very crumbly, especially first day.
I like a crispier cookie so I used all granulated sugar, melted butter, lowered the temperature and lengthened the cook time. They were AMAZING! Definitely my go-to😍
I did use monk fruit sweetener for the granulated sugar and whole wheat flour. But there’s peanut butter flavor comes through loud and clear!
I enjoy baking cookies and often made cookies for my children when they were young. I made these for my grandson and my daughter told me these were the best cookies I’ve ever made.
Easy to make and I added semi sweet chocolate chips
Absolutely delicious!!
